You cannot tell from that single sentence whether Alex has cancer. Inferring a specific health condition from “I have an appointment at the hospital next week” would be speculation about a sensitive health attribute and could be wrong and harmful.

Practical next steps you can take instead
- Ask Alex directly (respecting privacy) whether they’ll need time off or schedule changes.  
  Sample message you can send:
  "Hi Alex — I saw your note about an appointment at the hospital next week. I hope everything is okay. If you anticipate needing time off or any schedule changes, please let me know or tell me how we can support you. If you prefer to keep details private, that’s fine — just tell me what coverage you’ll need. Thanks."
- If needed, involve HR to handle sensitive employee-health matters and to ensure you follow legal/privacy policies.  
- Prepare a neutral staffing contingency (cross-train, temporary coverage, shift swaps) without assuming the reason for the appointment.

If you’d like, I can draft a shorter or more formal message to Alex or a template to share with HR. Which would you prefer?
